newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Dec state borrowing need seen 9.5 bln SKR.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Dec state borrowing need seen 9.5 bln SKR.

text.p: Sweden's state borrowing requirment for December was forecast On Monday at 9.5 billion crowns by the National Debt Office.
The office said its forecast for calendar 1996 was 26 billion crowns while the borrowing requirement for 1997 was forecast at 25-35 billion crowns.
The state borrowing need for November was seen at 7.8 billion crowns compared to a previous forecast of eight billion.
The borrowing requirement for October was confirmed at a credit of 4.6 billion crowns which was 2.3 billion crowns higher than the most recently published forecast.
"The increase in the borrowing requirement is due mainly to the higher cost of interest on the consolidated central grovenment debt," the debt office said.
The National Debt Office said it planned to issue four billion crowns in bonds in November and 14 billion crowns in bills.
It said it would issue two billion crowns of bonds and 24 billion crowns of bills in December.

"Borrowing during 1997 will be characterised by a relatively low net borrowing requirement coupled with a lower volume of outstanding bond loans maturing than in the previous year," the office said in a statement.
"Net borrowing in foreign currencies will be close to zero.
"The debt office expects to reduce the rate at which it issues index linked bonds."
The office said the total volume of nominal treasury bonds issued is expected to be slightly lower in 1997 than during the current year.
"The debt office does not at present foresee any changes in the volumes issued at auctions from the current two billion crowns," it said.
It said it still planned to introduce a new five-year treasury bond in the first quarter of 1997 as previously announced.
